In the meantime, University of Exeter staff and PGRs are always welcome to join the online sessions run by the Exeter Chaplaincy and there is other support available which is outlined on the page below. UoE Grief, Loss and Bereavement Group You can also contact the FX Plus Chaplaincy to arrange for pastoral support from one of their Chaplains. Close × Grief, Loss and Bereavement Group Monthly online session - Wednesdays Ad-hoc in-person sessions at St Lukes and Streatham campuses This group is led and supported by the University Chaplaincy (as facilitators with Cruse training) and Colleague Wellbeing. It is a support network for colleagues and PGRs experiencing any form of grief. loss or bereavement. You could be at any stage of this experience including, for example, a recent loss, a loss some time ago, facing the future loss of someone close, a miscarriage, or the 'loss' of someone still living in the case of advanced dementia where personality change and memory loss can be common. The group is a safe space for sharing/listening and practical/reflective activities with much mutual support. We have a Teams group to share useful thoughts, feelings and resources. Our in-person or online group sessions are informal, confidential and friendly. You do not need to commit to sessions in advance and can decide not to attend if feeling too raw. You don't have to speak or even have your camera on. All engage only a much as they want and is useful to them. More information, contact details, dates/ times and how to join the mailing/ invitation list: Grief, Loss and Bereavement Group Close × Exeter Writes The Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences' (HASS) Exeter Writes aims to create a better culture for writing and producing research across our community. Open to all staff and PGRs from HASS, ESE and HLS but get in touch if outside those faculties. A wide variety of writing retreats both on and off campus (including in Penryn), as well as writing and journalling workshops are now available throughout the academic year, along with a buddy system that pairs colleagues to support your writing. The team are always looking for new ideas and ways to support creative writing and practice. Please get in touch with your suggestions! Contact: Rachel Dallyn r.s.dallyn@exeter.ac.uk William Galois w.gallois@exeter.ac.uk Exeter Writes website Close × Hatha Yoga Tuesdays and Fridays 9.00 - 9.45am Classes are 45 minutes on Teams Cass Collins offers gentle yoga and meditation sessions to get you feeling more centred, calm and in control of your life. With more than 20 years experience practicing, studying and guiding students to a more balanced and flexible way of being you are in good hands on a journey from the head to the heart and beyond! If you have any concerns, would like more details or are new to the practice of yoga you are welcome to book a 15 minute introductory phone or video call. Email Cass with your preferred time, day and mobile number and she will book you in. Price For university staff and PGRs donations from £5 per class are welcomed. The usual price is £8 per session or pay in advance and commit to a whole month's worth of yoga (that's up to a max of 8 classes) for just £38, a saving of £26 per month. Fees should please be paid to the class instructor directly. Please email Cass to book your space and for payment options and see her socials for more information. cass@cassandracollins.co.uk Cass Collins Yoga on Facebook Instagram @cassandracollinsyoga Testimonial I have been joining Cass online for Kundalini yoga since the start of the pandemic. Cass is a wonderful and experienced yoga expert and the classes are fantastic. I simply love the classes, I always feel better, more positive and relaxed after the sessions and have become a Kundalini yoga convert – thanks to Cass. I cannot recommend yoga with Cass highly enough! Caroline Haughian Close × Healthy Cornwall Drop-in advice sessions covering a range of health and wellbeing topics, including offering a stop smoking service as well as diet, exercise, and general healthy lifestyle advice. For more info and joining details: Healthy Cornwall Close × International Staff & PG Network Are you an international member of staff or a PG student? Do you want to meet other international colleagues? Then join our network for International staff, all PG students and Post-docs. The aim of our group is to provide a space for people to connect, share experiences and information, and provide support to each other. We are planning to run monthly meetings on Teams, and we hope to have some face-to-face meetings on campus whenever possible. We would like to link to other like-minded groups at the university and in the community. Ideas are welcome! Contact: InternationalandPGnetwork@exeter.ac.uk Current information: International Staff and PG Network Close × Italian Reading Group Gruppo di lettura di italiano Fridays 1.35pm - 2.15pm 1H Queens, Streatham Campus An informal reading group for all learners and speakers of Italian. Do you speak Italian at an intermediate, advanced or native level? Allora vieni al gruppo di lettura! The reading group is open to everyone and feel free to bring your lunch. Contact for further info: Sonia Cunico s.cunico@exeter.ac.uk or Silvia Paloschi s.paloschi2@exeter.ac.uk Close × Kemeneth (Cornwall Cornwall LGBTQ+) Kemeneth (Cornish for ‘community’), the Cornwall LGBTQ+ Staff Network, welcomes all LGBTQ+ staff and allies at the University of Exeter Cornwall campuses, Falmouth University, FX Plus and The SU. Kemeneth was launched in 2023 to help create an inclusive environment for all sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions at our organisations and to celebrate the wonderfully diverse campus community we have in Cornwall. We are a safe space to get to know other members of the community both online and in-person, and will be hosting socials and events throughout the year. To join Kemeneth, and for more information: Kemeneth Close × Languages Café Join our informal conversation group for language speakers and enthusiasts of all levels. Open to all colleagues, PGRs and other University of Exeter students as well as members of the public. Practice your English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, BSL, Russian, Mandarin, Japanese and more. This free cafe is open to all colleagues, students, and the public. No sign up is required and tea and coffee will be provided. Contact: Samir Zarquane: s.zarqane@exeter.ac.uk Simon Breus: sb1067@exeter.ac.uk Close × LGBTQ+ Staff Network (Devon) We believe it's important to help create an inclusive environment for all sexual orientations and gender identities and expressions within the University. The Network is open to staff and PGRs of all marginalised sexual orientations and gender identities who would like a secure space to fully express their sexual orientation and/or gender without fear of intimidation or harassment. We also welcome those who do not identify as LGBTQ+ but would like to show their support for the LGBTQ+ community, are our allies and stand in solidarity with us. We run and promote a number of events, including a Coffee/Lunch Meet (running monthly, alternating between online and in-person on the Streatham campus). We also run more ad hoc events such as walks, game nights, and speaker events. Most events are open to all (including allies, and non-members), but some may hold space for specific groups. If you have queries or suggestions, or want to join as a coordinator, get in touch via email or our Sharepoint site. For more information about what we do and how, please see our full webpage where you will also find info on how to join the Network. LGBTQ+ Staff Network (Devon) Email: LGBTQPlusStaff@exeter.ac.uk Contact us: LBGTQ+ Sharepoint site Close × Menopause Café (Cornwall) All colleagues are invited to the Menopause Cafés, which will be held online and/or in-person monthly on our Penryn campus. The café lasts an hour and is an accessible, confidential, and supportive space colleagues can discuss any issues around menopause, gain signposting to further resources and support, and share information and tips. How to join? The Menopause Café is open to all Cornwall colleagues, whatever your gender or age. Note that the group is not open to students. Details of the cafés will be announced in Cornwall staff newsletters as well as via our Teams site. To join the Teams site or if you have any queries, please contact Clare Manser. Group Coordinators Clare Manser: C.manser@FXPlus.ac.uk Iris Ridout: iris.ridout@fxplus.ac.uk More information: Menopause Café (Cornwall) Please note that only colleagues based in Cornwall will be able to open the link. If you are based at a non-Cornwall campus and wish to join, please contact the organisers. Close × Menopause Network We are an informal, supportive group for staff members and students meeting every two months. Our menopause café-style sessions are a chance for anyone approaching or going through menopause, or who is post-menopausal, to meet and discuss whatever aspects of their experience they wish - brain fog, hot flushes, body changes, challenges to work and personal life. We also run a talk and Q&A each term (at least) from internal and external experts on, for example; HRT, nutrition, bone density, talking to GPs etc. For more information: Menopause guidance and Menopause Network Contact: Colleague Wellbeing Close × Multifaith Chaplaincy (FX Plus) Our chaplains are mostly of volunteers from local faith communities. They are very friendly and approachable and really care about what matters most to you. We will also do our best to connect you with someone of a specific faith community within the local area if you require. See our webpages for information on campus places of worship on and off campus (including at the Royal Cornwall Hospital) and for links to local faith communities! Do check our events pages as we have regular drop-in sessions and other ad-hoc events such as a craft group and lunches. We’re open to all. Email Address: chaplaincy@fxplus.ac.uk Phone Number: 01326370744 Close × Neurodiversity Café Following the success of the 2023 Neurodiversity Celebration Week events, we set up a new network for neurodivergent staff and PGR students. The Neurodiversity Café is a social group open to any staff member or PGR student who identifies as neurodivergent. We aim to create a neurodivergent-led, confidential and supportive space to meet regularly and talk about things that matter to us. We have a private Teams channel for informal chat and have regular body-doubling sessions. For more info on how to join see our webpage: Neurodiversity Café Contact: Lena Worwood s.worwood2@exeter.ac.uk Close × Parents and Carers Network (Cornwall) Primarily online communities where members can start conversations about any parenting, caring, or related questions; ask for advice from other members; and keep up to date with relevant information and policies. In-person meetings organised by members. Join the MS Teams site for current info . Guidance and support for parents and carers at the University of Exeter Close × Parents and Carers Network (Exeter) Primarily online communities where members can start conversations about any parenting, caring, or related questions; ask for advice from other members; and keep up to date with relevant information and policies. In-person meetings organised by members. Join the MS Teams site for current info . Close × Penryn Book Club Last Thursday of the month 12.00 We meet monthly, taking turns to choose a book. It’s super friendly, very informal, and literally everyone on the campus is invited. We read whatever is suggested, whether it’s fiction, non-fiction, memoir, genre, graphic novel, biography… anything. The only thing we try to stick to is that the book must be cheaply and readily available. We use a Padlet to organise ourselves then meet on the last Thursday of each month at 12 noon, somewhere on campus (Penryn). Everyone is welcome! To join please email Dan Bloomfield: d.bloomfield@exeter.ac.uk Close × Pilates & Menopause Pilates Mixed ability Pilates Monday @ 12.00pm Wednesday @ 9.00am Friday @ 9.00am Mixed ability, guided, online Pilates class with Rebecca who has delivered classes to University staff and PGRs since 2014 with rave reviews. Pilates for the Menopause class Wednesday @ 7.30pm All classes are via Zoom This is a mixed ability class using light weights (please have light weights of 1-1.5kg) and resistance bands. The routine aims to build muscle strength, support bone health (bone density decreases after the menopause and exercise using weights is beneficial to maintaining density) through resistance training and weight-bearing exercises. These sessions also include balance exercises and breathing techniques. The class is designed for anyone experiencing peri-menopausal, menopausal or post-menopausal symptoms. Booking and payment To book please follow link: www.ivegotyourback.co.uk book-online or contact Rebecca direct: ivegotyourbackuk@gmail.com Important information Do wear suitable clothes for exercise, light coloured where possible (so I can see you), have good lighting and position your mat lengthways across the screen (the way the mat is set up during class). The Pilates class will focus on the main phase of exercise so please ensure you have warmed up each major joint beforehand. Whilst this is a guided class and Becky can see you, she is not there to physically correct you. Please listen carefully to her instructions and to your bodies. Do not work through pain. Listen to your body, adapt, and if necessary, stop, stretch and reset. Please notify Rebecca before the class if you have any medical conditions or injuries. Close × Playful Lab Monthly(ish) The playful lab is an informal get-together for experimentation and exploration of the art and science of design, play, and story, to enable innovation. With play we create spaces to think, create, and level-up skills and understanding of learning and innovation while simultaneously fostering prosocial connection. For us, play is more than an activity, it is a feeling. Sign up here to receive calendar invites to our on-campus/ University sessions, receive our InnoPlay newsletter and for information on our other activites: www.innoplay.co.uk Close × Research Coding Community Do you design, support, or otherwise participate in computer coding for research activities? Are you an expert in, or new to Python, R, or some other coding language? A new Research Coding Community has recently been established, and you are invited to join for seminars, get-togethers, and friendly contests. Details of activities will feature here soon. We're currently gathering information about what members would like to do and when they are available. To express an interest in joining please contact Micheal Saunby and co-organisers via: rse-group@exeter.ac.uk Close × Research Networks The Exeter Research Networks are interdisciplinary, virtual research groupings. They bring together University of Exeter researchers and external partners to tackle pressing societal challenges. Check out their webpage to see current networks which might be relevant to you: Research Networks Close × Retired Staff Association Membership of the Association is open to all retired employees and retired former employees of the University, in all categories, including semi-retired employees. Various general social events take place throughout the year, including a Coffee Morning on the last Tuesday of most months. There are also a number of special interest groups who organize more specific activities. Currently the Association's membership includes very few retired members of staff based in Cornwall as its activities tend to be focused on the Exeter area and its Devon surroundings. However, special group outings do take members from time to time into Cornwall and UERSA would welcome an interest from potential Cornwall colleagues in extending its activities in the Duchy. For information more information on events and subscription: UERSA webpages Contacts: UERSA Committee Close × Role-Playing Games Social group to bring together staff from across St Lukes', Streatham and remotely who are interested in playing or running role-playing games. Do you find yourself daydreaming during your lunch break? Are you sick of the same old sandwiches? How about spending your lunch hour on fantastic adventures, telling stories and playing games with like-minded people? Role-playing games are one of the fastest-growing hobbies, with games like Dungeons and Dragons played by millions of people worldwide. Please jump straight onto our dedicated Discord server , introduce yourself, meet some like-minded colleagues and start playing some games! Games are taking place weekly or fortnightly in person and with the potential to run online as well. We are currently running role-playing games using: Dragon Age Dungeons and Dragons 5th Edition Pathfinder 1st Edition If you have any questions or want to know more: Pete Offord (via email or Teams) p.l.offord@exeter.ac.uk Close × School Governors Network Termly, usually on a Wednesday lunchtime between 12-1pm. Open to all campuses Online group The School and College Engagement team would like to extend an invitation to all colleagues who are currently acting as School Governors or Trustees in any discipline. They have established an online network to support governors and trustees with their work to share good practice, raise questions and find out more about how they can support them in their roles. There are termly meetings with guest speakers which provide a shared channel to debate pertinent topics and promote areas of discussion. If you would like to join the network, please get in touch: Contact: Sara Pittman s.pittman@exeter.ac.uk Close × Soapbox Science 2024 date - 22nd of June Exeter Quayside Soapbox Science showcases the research of women who are making significant contributions to the scientific community. The event, which takes place each summer, follows the format of London Hyde Park’s Speakers’ Corner, transforming an area of the city into an arena for public learning and scientific debate; creating a dynamic and bustling atmosphere and learning environment for all. For more information on this year’s plans and how to get involved as a presenter or volunteer see our Exeter webpage! Speakers from our Cornwall campuses are welcome too! Exeter Soapbox webpage Central Soapbox Science website You Tube: What is Soapbox Science? Close × Soup Lunch Thursdays from 12.30 to 2pm Come and enjoy a FREE LUNCH of soup and bread served by our Chaplains. Every Thursday during term-time on First Floor of Staff House. Vegetarian and vegan options will be available. Drop in any time. People from all faiths or none are warmly welcomed. More information on the Chaplaincy, other events and the Connections cafe: UoE Chaplaincy Contact: chaplaincy@exeter.ac.uk Close × Sports Park memberships and activities Explore University of Exeter gym, swim and classes membership options and fitness classes. Close × Luke'sCraft In-person South Cloisters, St Luke's Campus Every Tuesday, 12:30-13:00 Our friendly craft group has restarted, bring your own craft or use our wool supplies! Contact: Sue Whiffin s.m.whiffin@exeter.ac.uk Close × St Luke's Volunteer Gardening Group (SLUG) Wednesday lunchtimes 12.00-14.00 Everyone at St Luke’s, both staff and students, is welcome to join this group to help with the redesigning and uplifting of an area of St Luke’s campus to enhance wellbeing by providing a quiet space for staff and students to interact with green spaces and each other. Come along and do as much or as little as you like – just come and enjoy the space! The Garden can be found behind South Cloisters and is accessed by a pathway on the left-hand side just before the black side gates onto College Road. If you would like to be added to the email distribution list and be kept updated with developments, plans, events (cake sales, bulb planting etc.) please email us. Contact: StLukes_Volunteer_Garden@exeter.ac.uk Close × Tai Chi Mondays 12.30 - 13.20 There is an open, online lunchtime Chi-break class using Zoom, occasionally with a room booked on Streatham campus for staff to meet in person. Staff and students from any University of Exeter campus are welcome to join these sessions. Please note that the online class is also open to non-university members. The cost for the online classes is £7/class. Payments should please be paid to the class instructor directly.The best way to receive information about the classes, payment and Zoom details is to subscribe to the Living Movement newsletter. Please go to the Living Movement website to sign up for the newsletter. The moves of Tai Chi and Qigong are easy to learn and the low impact workout leaves you feeling good in body and mind. The classes will include gentle exercises, key moves and a little bit of short form. The classes are run by Angus Clark who is an experienced instructor, author and honorary vice-president of the Tai Chi Union of Great Britain. His website is www.livingmovement.com Contact: Anke Djordjevic a.djordjevic@exeter.ac.uk Kathryn Fyfe k.v.s.fyfe@exeter.ac.uk Close × Trans and Non-Binary Café At the Trans and Non-binary Café we offer a chance to come together with other trans people and discuss whatever you would like. Usually at some point being trans comes up but we believe there’s great value in being with other trans people, having a chance to catch up and talk and make friends with people who share the same sorts of experiences. We run a private Discord server and hold monthly in-person meetings at a wheelchair accessible location on campus. We don't share the venue or discord link publicly to protect the privacy of members but you can get these by emailing transcafe@exeter.ac.uk or if you are already in it, in the Discord server. If you are nervous of coming and would like support with it, or if you have any other questions, please do get in touch with transcafe@exeter.ac.uk, where someone from our small, all trans organising team will be happy to help. Contact: transcafe@exeter.ac.uk For more detailed information: Trans and Non-Binary Café Close × University Choral Society Mondays 7-9pm Mary Harris Memorial Chapel Open to students, staff and members of the public and welcomes singers of all levels of ability. Rehearsals are Monday evenings from 7:00-9:00pm in the Mary Harris Memorial Chapel on the Streatham Campus. Each term we hold concerts of large choral works often accompanied by student orchestras such as the University Symphony Orchestra and the University Chamber Orchestra. More info and joining instructions including memberships needed which are different for staff than for PGRs who will count as students: University Choral Society Instagram page @uoechoralsoc Close × Vegan & Vegetarian Meet-up Mondays 11.30-12.00 Term-time with ad-hoc meet-ups outside term. Hello Vegans and Vegetarian staff at the University of Exeter!!!! Let’s get together outside Reed hall (the seating area outside the cafe) at to have a chat about our experience of being vegan and/ or vegetarian in Exeter!! If the weather is nice, we can go for a little stroll around Reed pond! If wet we'll meet in the cafe inside. Get in touch to join the mailing list or for more information. Contact: Preethy Grima p.grima@exeter.ac.uk Close × Wellbeing Network We are a volunteer-led social community aiming to improve our wellbeing through positive activities and open conversations about mental health. We have a Teams group for connecting as and when, organise social "Fika" meet-ups, and other ad-hoc wellbeing positive events and activities e.g. Swing dance and yoga tasters! It's about: Open-minded conversations about how you are really feeling and doing. An opportunity for social connection. A supportive environment where all feel welcome. An invitation to come along to activities and socials. For more information about the group and our activities, to join, or to get in touch about helping us run the group see our webpage: Wellbeing Network Close × WISEnet (Women: Inspiring, Supporting, Encouraging Network) Online, hybrid and in-person Various days A new network for women has launched this year to bring together women and allies across our community. The Women: Inspiring, Supporting, Encouraging Network (WISEnet) is an inclusive and welcoming space for all women, including trans women and non-binary colleagues, to discuss relevant topics and benefit from the activities supported by the group. The network also welcomes male allies and is open to anyone that can advocate for gender equality. We run termly speaker events and have a Teams site for discussion outside of meetings. Events are hybrid to allow as many people to attend as possible. The in-person aspect of these is at Streatham campus. Find out more: WISEnet webpage Contact: wisenetwork@exeter.ac.uk Close If a correction to this page is needed or you have a question, please contact: ColleagueWellbeing@exeter.ac.uk Using our site | Accessibility | Freedom of Information | Data Protection | Copyright & disclaimer | Privacy & cookies | Cookie settings Copyright University of Exeter . Groups, networks and activities | Current staff | University of Exeter Global links Home Study Research For business Alumni Departments Visit us About us Current students International students Current staff facebook youtube instagram Search Website links Home News and updates Weekly Bulletin Rumourbuster Staff talks Faculty news Make a difference HR and employment Your employment Benefits and recognition Colleague Wellbeing Equality, diversity and inclusion Groups, networks and activities Occupational Health Volunteering and giving A-Z of services and support Campus facilities Contacts Section links Home Current staff Groups, networks and activities Groups, networks and activities All University of Exeter colleagues (current, temporary, visiting and retired) and PGRs from any of our campuses, are welcome to participate in the groups and activities listed on these pages. The fully searchable list below includes groups, networks and other activities from all campuses including ones which are online only. You could browse the whole list to see what tickles your fancy, or do a search using one of the following in the search box below and then click on the group name for more detailed information on joining etc. Campus name or broad location e.g. "Cornwall" or "St Lukes". "Online", "hybrid" or "all" for ones you can join in with from anywhere. Topic/ activity/ keyword if looking for a group on particular subject e.g. "craft" or "School Governors". Day of the week. Note - some groups may not have a set day, meet only monthly or may have activities at the weekend e.g. Hiking. Adding an existing group to this list We're happy to add existing staff-led groups that don't currently feature here unless they are one of our Research Networks as they have their own page! It's also ok to add a PGR-led group as long as it's open to staff members too. See the next section though if you want guidance on setting up a brand new group from scratch. To an existing group or network added, please get in touch via email digitalteam@exeter.ac.uk providing key information including: Name of the group, network or activity When, where and how frequently you meet up Is this in-person? If so which campus/es? Online only? Hybrid? A link to your webpages if you have one A contact email address for the listing and a name if possible Name and direct email address for the admin of this page so we can contact you regarding periodic updates. Setting up a new group You will be responsible for running the group at an administrative and practical level. This includes advertising and looking after a web page if your group has one. We'll contact you annually to check the details of your group. Please need to let us know if the regular day and time for your activities changes so we can amend the timetable/overview of all social groups. Setting up a Sharepoint site/ Teams group is a useful way to organise many groups and communicate in a more fluid way than a simple email list but this depends on the type of group you're running and what kind of admin skills/ access you have. Information is linked here on how to set up a Microsoft Teams group but contact IT if you need further support on this. We can give some advice in setting up the group and advertising if you get stuck. Some FAQs are being developed and will be added to this page as soon as they are ready. We do not usually set up webpages for individual groups. We sometimes include mention of groups in Colleague Wellbeing weekly bulletin items if it links to a campaign we are running and will contact you when we're thinking of doing this. If you wish to do a promotion drive or have a special event coming up please do get in touch. Colleague Wellbeing has no current access to budget for funding groups or other setup costs. If the group incurs costs e.g. for an instructor, this needs to be covered by the members and administration of that should be looked after by the group itself. You'll need to book your own rooms or space to run activities and carry-out any necessary risk assessments. However, do contact us if guidance or assistance is needed as we have good knowledge of University spaces and procedures at Streatham and St Lukes. Who can do this? Any PGR or staff member can set up a group on any campus. It's a good idea to make sure there enough interest from other colleagues first - we suggest a minimum of 6 people will be needed. One way to do this is to put something into the weekly bulletin asking people to get in touch with you (via email, Teams or a webform) if they are interested. Students, staff, and local residents are all welcome to join, no skills are necessary, just an interest and enthusiasm. We hold occasional social and fundraising events too. Exeter Community Garden started in 2011 as a joint initiative between the University’s grounds team and the Students’ Guild and has now evolved into a free-standing organisation managed by staff, students and local residents. The garden has 9 raised beds for vegetables, fruit and herbs, an orchard with a variety of fruit trees, together with a greenhouse, a storage building (the Observatory) and two polytunnels. As well as producing food, the Garden allows members to share skills and ideas, promotes mental wellbeing through social interaction and also allows members to look at issues of food security and sustainability, habitat protection and enhancement and the promotion of biodiversity. The Community Garden has engaged with students and academics at the University to launch the Permaculture, Growing Food with Nature MA in Food Studies based on the community garden site and using the facilities here. The course specifically investigates food production without cultivation, using sustainable products. The term "fika" is derived from the Swedish word "kaffe" (coffee) and is akin to the concept of a coffee break or coffee time, but it goes beyond just drinking coffee. Close × Grief, Loss and Bereavement Group Monthly online session - Wednesdays Ad-hoc in-person sessions at St Lukes and Streatham campuses This group is led and supported by the University Chaplaincy (as facilitators with Cruse training) and Colleague Wellbeing. It is a support network for colleagues and PGRs experiencing any form of grief. loss or bereavement. You could be at any stage of this experience including, for example, a recent loss, a loss some time ago, facing the future loss of someone close, a miscarriage, or the 'loss' of someone still living in the case of advanced dementia where personality change and memory loss can be common. The group is a safe space for sharing/listening and practical/reflective activities with much mutual support. We have a Teams group to share useful thoughts, feelings and resources. Our in-person or online group sessions are informal, confidential and friendly. You do not need to commit to sessions in advance and can decide not to attend if feeling too raw. You don't have to speak or even have your camera on. All engage only a much as they want and is useful to them. It’s super friendly, very informal, and literally everyone on the campus is invited. We read whatever is suggested, whether it’s fiction, non-fiction, memoir, genre, graphic novel, biography… anything. The only thing we try to stick to is that the book must be cheaply and readily available. We use a Padlet to organise ourselves then meet on the last Thursday of each month at 12 noon, somewhere on campus (Penryn). Everyone is welcome! To join please email Dan Bloomfield: d.bloomfield@exeter.ac.uk Close × Pilates & Menopause Pilates Mixed ability Pilates Monday @ 12.00pm Wednesday @ 9.00am Friday @ 9.00am Mixed ability, guided, online Pilates class with Rebecca who has delivered classes to University staff and PGRs since 2014 with rave reviews. Pilates for the Menopause class Wednesday @ 7.30pm All classes are via Zoom This is a mixed ability class using light weights (please have light weights of 1-1.5kg) and resistance bands. The routine aims to build muscle strength, support bone health (bone density decreases after the menopause and exercise using weights is beneficial to maintaining density) through resistance training and weight-bearing exercises. These sessions also include balance exercises and breathing techniques. The class is designed for anyone experiencing peri-menopausal, menopausal or post-menopausal symptoms. Booking and payment To book please follow link: www.ivegotyourback.co.uk book-online or contact Rebecca direct: ivegotyourbackuk@gmail.com Important information Do wear suitable clothes for exercise, light coloured where possible (so I can see you), have good lighting and position your mat lengthways across the screen (the way the mat is set up during class). The Pilates class will focus on the main phase of exercise so please ensure you have warmed up each major joint beforehand. Whilst this is a guided class and Becky can see you, she is not there to physically correct you. Please listen carefully to her instructions and to your bodies. Do not work through pain. Listen to your body, adapt, and if necessary, stop, stretch and reset. Please notify Rebecca before the class if you have any medical conditions or injuries. For us, play is more than an activity, it is a feeling. Sign up here to receive calendar invites to our on-campus/ University sessions, receive our InnoPlay newsletter and for information on our other activites: www.innoplay.co.uk Close × Research Coding Community Do you design, support, or otherwise participate in computer coding for research activities? Are you an expert in, or new to Python, R, or some other coding language? A new Research Coding Community has recently been established, and you are invited to join for seminars, get-togethers, and friendly contests. Details of activities will feature here soon. We're currently gathering information about what members would like to do and when they are available. To express an interest in joining please contact Micheal Saunby and co-organisers via: rse-group@exeter.ac.uk Close × Research Networks The Exeter Research Networks are interdisciplinary, virtual research groupings. They bring together University of Exeter researchers and external partners to tackle pressing societal challenges. Check out their webpage to see current networks which might be relevant to you: Research Networks Close × Retired Staff Association Membership of the Association is open to all retired employees and retired former employees of the University, in all categories, including semi-retired employees. Various general social events take place throughout the year, including a Coffee Morning on the last Tuesday of most months. There are also a number of special interest groups who organize more specific activities. Currently the Association's membership includes very few retired members of staff based in Cornwall as its activities tend to be focused on the Exeter area and its Devon surroundings. However, special group outings do take members from time to time into Cornwall and UERSA would welcome an interest from potential Cornwall colleagues in extending its activities in the Duchy. For information more information on events and subscription: UERSA webpages Contacts: UERSA Committee Close × Role-Playing Games Social group to bring together staff from across St Lukes', Streatham and remotely who are interested in playing or running role-playing games. Do you find yourself daydreaming during your lunch break? Are you sick of the same old sandwiches? How about spending your lunch hour on fantastic adventures, telling stories and playing games with like-minded people? Role-playing games are one of the fastest-growing hobbies, with games like Dungeons and Dragons played by millions of people worldwide. Please jump straight onto our dedicated Discord server , introduce yourself, meet some like-minded colleagues and start playing some games! Games are taking place weekly or fortnightly in person and with the potential to run online as well. We are currently running role-playing games using: Dragon Age Dungeons and Dragons 5th Edition Pathfinder 1st Edition If you have any questions or want to know more: Pete Offord (via email or Teams) p.l.offord@exeter.ac.uk Close × School Governors Network Termly, usually on a Wednesday lunchtime between 12-1pm. Open to all campuses Online group The School and College Engagement team would like to extend an invitation to all colleagues who are currently acting as School Governors or Trustees in any discipline. They have established an online network to support governors and trustees with their work to share good practice, raise questions and find out more about how they can support them in their roles. There are termly meetings with guest speakers which provide a shared channel to debate pertinent topics and promote areas of discussion. Exeter Soapbox webpage Central Soapbox Science website You Tube: What is Soapbox Science? Contact: StLukes_Volunteer_Garden@exeter.ac.uk Close × Tai Chi Mondays 12.30 - 13.20 There is an open, online lunchtime Chi-break class using Zoom, occasionally with a room booked on Streatham campus for staff to meet in person. Staff and students from any University of Exeter campus are welcome to join these sessions. Please note that the online class is also open to non-university members. The cost for the online classes is £7/class. Payments should please be paid to the class instructor directly.The best way to receive information about the classes, payment and Zoom details is to subscribe to the Living Movement newsletter. Please go to the Living Movement website to sign up for the newsletter. The moves of Tai Chi and Qigong are easy to learn and the low impact workout leaves you feeling good in body and mind. The classes will include gentle exercises, key moves and a little bit of short form. The classes are run by Angus Clark who is an experienced instructor, author and honorary vice-president of the Tai Chi Union of Great Britain. We run a private Discord server and hold monthly in-person meetings at a wheelchair accessible location on campus. We don't share the venue or discord link publicly to protect the privacy of members but you can get these by emailing transcafe@exeter.ac.uk or if you are already in it, in the Discord server. If you are nervous of coming and would like support with it, or if you have any other questions, please do get in touch with transcafe@exeter.ac.uk, where someone from our small, all trans organising team will be happy to help. The fully searchable list below includes groups, networks and other activities from all campuses including ones which are online only. You could browse the whole list to see what tickles your fancy, or do a search using one of the following in the search box below and then click on the group name for more detailed information on joining etc. Campus name or broad location e.g. "Cornwall" or "St Lukes". "Online", "hybrid" or "all" for ones you can join in with from anywhere. Topic/ activity/ keyword if looking for a group on particular subject e.g. "craft" or "School Governors". Day of the week. Note - some groups may not have a set day, meet only monthly or may have activities at the weekend e.g. Hiking. Adding an existing group to this list We're happy to add existing staff-led groups that don't currently feature here unless they are one of our Research Networks as they have their own page! It's also ok to add a PGR-led group as long as it's open to staff members too. See the next section though if you want guidance on setting up a brand new group from scratch. To an existing group or network added, please get in touch via email digitalteam@exeter.ac.uk providing key information including: Name of the group, network or activity When, where and how frequently you meet up Is this in-person? If so which campus/es? Online only? Hybrid? A link to your webpages if you have one A contact email address for the listing and a name if possible Name and direct email address for the admin of this page so we can contact you regarding periodic updates. Setting up a new group You will be responsible for running the group at an administrative and practical level. This includes advertising and looking after a web page if your group has one. We'll contact you annually to check the details of your group. Please need to let us know if the regular day and time for your activities changes so we can amend the timetable/overview of all social groups. Setting up a Sharepoint site/ Teams group is a useful way to organise many groups and communicate in a more fluid way than a simple email list but this depends on the type of group you're running and what kind of admin skills/ access you have. Information is linked here on how to set up a Microsoft Teams group but contact IT if you need further support on this. We can give some advice in setting up the group and advertising if you get stuck. Some FAQs are being developed and will be added to this page as soon as they are ready. We do not usually set up webpages for individual groups. We sometimes include mention of groups in Colleague Wellbeing weekly bulletin items if it links to a campaign we are running and will contact you when we're thinking of doing this. If you wish to do a promotion drive or have a special event coming up please do get in touch. Colleague Wellbeing has no current access to budget for funding groups or other setup costs. If the group incurs costs e.g. for an instructor, this needs to be covered by the members and administration of that should be looked after by the group itself. You'll need to book your own rooms or space to run activities and carry-out any necessary risk assessments. However, do contact us if guidance or assistance is needed as we have good knowledge of University spaces and procedures at Streatham and St Lukes. Who can do this? Any PGR or staff member can set up a group on any campus. It's a good idea to make sure there enough interest from other colleagues first - we suggest a minimum of 6 people will be needed. One way to do this is to put something into the weekly bulletin asking people to get in touch with you (via email, Teams or a webform) if they are interested. The fully searchable list below includes groups, networks and other activities from all campuses including ones which are online only. You could browse the whole list to see what tickles your fancy, or do a search using one of the following in the search box below and then click on the group name for more detailed information on joining etc. Campus name or broad location e.g. "Cornwall" or "St Lukes". "Online", "hybrid" or "all" for ones you can join in with from anywhere. Topic/ activity/ keyword if looking for a group on particular subject e.g. "craft" or "School Governors". Day of the week. Note - some groups may not have a set day, meet only monthly or may have activities at the weekend e.g. Hiking. Adding an existing group to this list We're happy to add existing staff-led groups that don't currently feature here unless they are one of our Research Networks as they have their own page! It's also ok to add a PGR-led group as long as it's open to staff members too. See the next section though if you want guidance on setting up a brand new group from scratch. To an existing group or network added, please get in touch via email digitalteam@exeter.ac.uk providing key information including: Name of the group, network or activity When, where and how frequently you meet up Is this in-person? If so which campus/es? Online only? Hybrid? A link to your webpages if you have one A contact email address for the listing and a name if possible Name and direct email address for the admin of this page so we can contact you regarding periodic updates. Setting up a new group You will be responsible for running the group at an administrative and practical level. This includes advertising and looking after a web page if your group has one. We'll contact you annually to check the details of your group. Please need to let us know if the regular day and time for your activities changes so we can amend the timetable/overview of all social groups. Setting up a Sharepoint site/ Teams group is a useful way to organise many groups and communicate in a more fluid way than a simple email list but this depends on the type of group you're running and what kind of admin skills/ access you have. Information is linked here on how to set up a Microsoft Teams group but contact IT if you need further support on this. We can give some advice in setting up the group and advertising if you get stuck. Some FAQs are being developed and will be added to this page as soon as they are ready. We do not usually set up webpages for individual groups. We sometimes include mention of groups in Colleague Wellbeing weekly bulletin items if it links to a campaign we are running and will contact you when we're thinking of doing this. If you wish to do a promotion drive or have a special event coming up please do get in touch. Colleague Wellbeing has no current access to budget for funding groups or other setup costs. If the group incurs costs e.g. for an instructor, this needs to be covered by the members and administration of that should be looked after by the group itself. You'll need to book your own rooms or space to run activities and carry-out any necessary risk assessments. However, do contact us if guidance or assistance is needed as we have good knowledge of University spaces and procedures at Streatham and St Lukes. Who can do this? Any PGR or staff member can set up a group on any campus. It's a good idea to make sure there enough interest from other colleagues first - we suggest a minimum of 6 people will be needed. One way to do this is to put something into the weekly bulletin asking people to get in touch with you (via email, Teams or a webform) if they are interested. In the meantime, University of Exeter staff and PGRs are always welcome to join the online sessions run by the Exeter Chaplaincy and there is other support available which is outlined on the page below. UoE Grief, Loss and Bereavement Group You can also contact the FX Plus Chaplaincy to arrange for pastoral support from one of their Chaplains. Close × Grief, Loss and Bereavement Group Monthly online session - Wednesdays Ad-hoc in-person sessions at St Lukes and Streatham campuses This group is led and supported by the University Chaplaincy (as facilitators with Cruse training) and Colleague Wellbeing. It is a support network for colleagues and PGRs experiencing any form of grief. loss or bereavement. You could be at any stage of this experience including, for example, a recent loss, a loss some time ago, facing the future loss of someone close, a miscarriage, or the 'loss' of someone still living in the case of advanced dementia where personality change and memory loss can be common. The group is a safe space for sharing/listening and practical/reflective activities with much mutual support. We have a Teams group to share useful thoughts, feelings and resources. Our in-person or online group sessions are informal, confidential and friendly. You do not need to commit to sessions in advance and can decide not to attend if feeling too raw. You don't have to speak or even have your camera on. All engage only a much as they want and is useful to them. More information, contact details, dates/ times and how to join the mailing/ invitation list: Grief, Loss and Bereavement Group Close × Exeter Writes The Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences' (HASS) Exeter Writes aims to create a better culture for writing and producing research across our community. Open to all staff and PGRs from HASS, ESE and HLS but get in touch if outside those faculties. A wide variety of writing retreats both on and off campus (including in Penryn), as well as writing and journalling workshops are now available throughout the academic year, along with a buddy system that pairs colleagues to support your writing. The team are always looking for new ideas and ways to support creative writing and practice. Please get in touch with your suggestions! Contact: Rachel Dallyn r.s.dallyn@exeter.ac.uk William Galois w.gallois@exeter.ac.uk Exeter Writes website Close × Hatha Yoga Tuesdays and Fridays 9.00 - 9.45am Classes are 45 minutes on Teams Cass Collins offers gentle yoga and meditation sessions to get you feeling more centred, calm and in control of your life. With more than 20 years experience practicing, studying and guiding students to a more balanced and flexible way of being you are in good hands on a journey from the head to the heart and beyond! If you have any concerns, would like more details or are new to the practice of yoga you are welcome to book a 15 minute introductory phone or video call. Email Cass with your preferred time, day and mobile number and she will book you in. Price For university staff and PGRs donations from £5 per class are welcomed. The usual price is £8 per session or pay in advance and commit to a whole month's worth of yoga (that's up to a max of 8 classes) for just £38, a saving of £26 per month. Fees should please be paid to the class instructor directly. Please email Cass to book your space and for payment options and see her socials for more information. cass@cassandracollins.co.uk Cass Collins Yoga on Facebook Instagram @cassandracollinsyoga Testimonial I have been joining Cass online for Kundalini yoga since the start of the pandemic. Cass is a wonderful and experienced yoga expert and the classes are fantastic. I simply love the classes, I always feel better, more positive and relaxed after the sessions and have become a Kundalini yoga convert – thanks to Cass. I cannot recommend yoga with Cass highly enough! Caroline Haughian Close × Healthy Cornwall Drop-in advice sessions covering a range of health and wellbeing topics, including offering a stop smoking service as well as diet, exercise, and general healthy lifestyle advice. For more info and joining details: Healthy Cornwall Close × International Staff & PG Network Are you an international member of staff or a PG student? Do you want to meet other international colleagues? Then join our network for International staff, all PG students and Post-docs. The aim of our group is to provide a space for people to connect, share experiences and information, and provide support to each other. We are planning to run monthly meetings on Teams, and we hope to have some face-to-face meetings on campus whenever possible. We would like to link to other like-minded groups at the university and in the community. Ideas are welcome! Contact: InternationalandPGnetwork@exeter.ac.uk Current information: International Staff and PG Network Close × Italian Reading Group Gruppo di lettura di italiano Fridays 1.35pm - 2.15pm 1H Queens, Streatham Campus An informal reading group for all learners and speakers of Italian. Do you speak Italian at an intermediate, advanced or native level? Allora vieni al gruppo di lettura! The reading group is open to everyone and feel free to bring your lunch. Contact for further info: Sonia Cunico s.cunico@exeter.ac.uk or Silvia Paloschi s.paloschi2@exeter.ac.uk Close × Kemeneth (Cornwall Cornwall LGBTQ+) Kemeneth (Cornish for ‘community’), the Cornwall LGBTQ+ Staff Network, welcomes all LGBTQ+ staff and allies at the University of Exeter Cornwall campuses, Falmouth University, FX Plus and The SU. Kemeneth was launched in 2023 to help create an inclusive environment for all sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions at our organisations and to celebrate the wonderfully diverse campus community we have in Cornwall. We are a safe space to get to know other members of the community both online and in-person, and will be hosting socials and events throughout the year. To join Kemeneth, and for more information: Kemeneth Close × Languages Café Join our informal conversation group for language speakers and enthusiasts of all levels. Open to all colleagues, PGRs and other University of Exeter students as well as members of the public. Practice your English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Arabic, BSL, Russian, Mandarin, Japanese and more. This free cafe is open to all colleagues, students, and the public. No sign up is required and tea and coffee will be provided. Contact: Samir Zarquane: s.zarqane@exeter.ac.uk Simon Breus: sb1067@exeter.ac.uk Close × LGBTQ+ Staff Network (Devon) We believe it's important to help create an inclusive environment for all sexual orientations and gender identities and expressions within the University. The Network is open to staff and PGRs of all marginalised sexual orientations and gender identities who would like a secure space to fully express their sexual orientation and/or gender without fear of intimidation or harassment. We also welcome those who do not identify as LGBTQ+ but would like to show their support for the LGBTQ+ community, are our allies and stand in solidarity with us. We run and promote a number of events, including a Coffee/Lunch Meet (running monthly, alternating between online and in-person on the Streatham campus). We also run more ad hoc events such as walks, game nights, and speaker events. Most events are open to all (including allies, and non-members), but some may hold space for specific groups. If you have queries or suggestions, or want to join as a coordinator, get in touch via email or our Sharepoint site. For more information about what we do and how, please see our full webpage where you will also find info on how to join the Network. LGBTQ+ Staff Network (Devon) Email: LGBTQPlusStaff@exeter.ac.uk Contact us: LBGTQ+ Sharepoint site Close × Menopause Café (Cornwall) All colleagues are invited to the Menopause Cafés, which will be held online and/or in-person monthly on our Penryn campus. The café lasts an hour and is an accessible, confidential, and supportive space colleagues can discuss any issues around menopause, gain signposting to further resources and support, and share information and tips. How to join? The Menopause Café is open to all Cornwall colleagues, whatever your gender or age. Note that the group is not open to students. Details of the cafés will be announced in Cornwall staff newsletters as well as via our Teams site. To join the Teams site or if you have any queries, please contact Clare Manser. Group Coordinators Clare Manser: C.manser@FXPlus.ac.uk Iris Ridout: iris.ridout@fxplus.ac.uk More information: Menopause Café (Cornwall) Please note that only colleagues based in Cornwall will be able to open the link. If you are based at a non-Cornwall campus and wish to join, please contact the organisers. Close × Menopause Network We are an informal, supportive group for staff members and students meeting every two months. Our menopause café-style sessions are a chance for anyone approaching or going through menopause, or who is post-menopausal, to meet and discuss whatever aspects of their experience they wish - brain fog, hot flushes, body changes, challenges to work and personal life. We also run a talk and Q&A each term (at least) from internal and external experts on, for example; HRT, nutrition, bone density, talking to GPs etc. For more information: Menopause guidance and Menopause Network Contact: Colleague Wellbeing Close × Multifaith Chaplaincy (FX Plus) Our chaplains are mostly of volunteers from local faith communities. They are very friendly and approachable and really care about what matters most to you. We will also do our best to connect you with someone of a specific faith community within the local area if you require. See our webpages for information on campus places of worship on and off campus (including at the Royal Cornwall Hospital) and for links to local faith communities! Do check our events pages as we have regular drop-in sessions and other ad-hoc events such as a craft group and lunches. We’re open to all. Email Address: chaplaincy@fxplus.ac.uk Phone Number: 01326370744 Close × Neurodiversity Café Following the success of the 2023 Neurodiversity Celebration Week events, we set up a new network for neurodivergent staff and PGR students. The Neurodiversity Café is a social group open to any staff member or PGR student who identifies as neurodivergent. We aim to create a neurodivergent-led, confidential and supportive space to meet regularly and talk about things that matter to us. We have a private Teams channel for informal chat and have regular body-doubling sessions. For more info on how to join see our webpage: Neurodiversity Café Contact: Lena Worwood s.worwood2@exeter.ac.uk Close × Parents and Carers Network (Cornwall) Primarily online communities where members can start conversations about any parenting, caring, or related questions; ask for advice from other members; and keep up to date with relevant information and policies. In-person meetings organised by members. Join the MS Teams site for current info . Guidance and support for parents and carers at the University of Exeter Close × Parents and Carers Network (Exeter) Primarily online communities where members can start conversations about any parenting, caring, or related questions; ask for advice from other members; and keep up to date with relevant information and policies. In-person meetings organised by members. Join the MS Teams site for current info . Close × Penryn Book Club Last Thursday of the month 12.00 We meet monthly, taking turns to choose a book. It’s super friendly, very informal, and literally everyone on the campus is invited. We read whatever is suggested, whether it’s fiction, non-fiction, memoir, genre, graphic novel, biography… anything. The only thing we try to stick to is that the book must be cheaply and readily available. We use a Padlet to organise ourselves then meet on the last Thursday of each month at 12 noon, somewhere on campus (Penryn). Everyone is welcome! To join please email Dan Bloomfield: d.bloomfield@exeter.ac.uk Close × Pilates & Menopause Pilates Mixed ability Pilates Monday @ 12.00pm Wednesday @ 9.00am Friday @ 9.00am Mixed ability, guided, online Pilates class with Rebecca who has delivered classes to University staff and PGRs since 2014 with rave reviews. Pilates for the Menopause class Wednesday @ 7.30pm All classes are via Zoom This is a mixed ability class using light weights (please have light weights of 1-1.5kg) and resistance bands. The routine aims to build muscle strength, support bone health (bone density decreases after the menopause and exercise using weights is beneficial to maintaining density) through resistance training and weight-bearing exercises. These sessions also include balance exercises and breathing techniques. The class is designed for anyone experiencing peri-menopausal, menopausal or post-menopausal symptoms. Booking and payment To book please follow link: www.ivegotyourback.co.uk book-online or contact Rebecca direct: ivegotyourbackuk@gmail.com Important information Do wear suitable clothes for exercise, light coloured where possible (so I can see you), have good lighting and position your mat lengthways across the screen (the way the mat is set up during class). The Pilates class will focus on the main phase of exercise so please ensure you have warmed up each major joint beforehand. Whilst this is a guided class and Becky can see you, she is not there to physically correct you. Please listen carefully to her instructions and to your bodies. Do not work through pain. Listen to your body, adapt, and if necessary, stop, stretch and reset. Please notify Rebecca before the class if you have any medical conditions or injuries. Close × Playful Lab Monthly(ish) The playful lab is an informal get-together for experimentation and exploration of the art and science of design, play, and story, to enable innovation. With play we create spaces to think, create, and level-up skills and understanding of learning and innovation while simultaneously fostering prosocial connection. For us, play is more than an activity, it is a feeling. Sign up here to receive calendar invites to our on-campus/ University sessions, receive our InnoPlay newsletter and for information on our other activites: www.innoplay.co.uk Close × Research Coding Community Do you design, support, or otherwise participate in computer coding for research activities? Are you an expert in, or new to Python, R, or some other coding language? A new Research Coding Community has recently been established, and you are invited to join for seminars, get-togethers, and friendly contests. Details of activities will feature here soon. We're currently gathering information about what members would like to do and when they are available. To express an interest in joining please contact Micheal Saunby and co-organisers via: rse-group@exeter.ac.uk Close × Research Networks The Exeter Research Networks are interdisciplinary, virtual research groupings. They bring together University of Exeter researchers and external partners to tackle pressing societal challenges. Check out their webpage to see current networks which might be relevant to you: Research Networks Close × Retired Staff Association Membership of the Association is open to all retired employees and retired former employees of the University, in all categories, including semi-retired employees. Various general social events take place throughout the year, including a Coffee Morning on the last Tuesday of most months. There are also a number of special interest groups who organize more specific activities. Currently the Association's membership includes very few retired members of staff based in Cornwall as its activities tend to be focused on the Exeter area and its Devon surroundings. However, special group outings do take members from time to time into Cornwall and UERSA would welcome an interest from potential Cornwall colleagues in extending its activities in the Duchy. For information more information on events and subscription: UERSA webpages Contacts: UERSA Committee Close × Role-Playing Games Social group to bring together staff from across St Lukes', Streatham and remotely who are interested in playing or running role-playing games. Do you find yourself daydreaming during your lunch break? Are you sick of the same old sandwiches? How about spending your lunch hour on fantastic adventures, telling stories and playing games with like-minded people? Role-playing games are one of the fastest-growing hobbies, with games like Dungeons and Dragons played by millions of people worldwide. Please jump straight onto our dedicated Discord server , introduce yourself, meet some like-minded colleagues and start playing some games! Games are taking place weekly or fortnightly in person and with the potential to run online as well. We are currently running role-playing games using: Dragon Age Dungeons and Dragons 5th Edition Pathfinder 1st Edition If you have any questions or want to know more: Pete Offord (via email or Teams) p.l.offord@exeter.ac.uk Close × School Governors Network Termly, usually on a Wednesday lunchtime between 12-1pm. Open to all campuses Online group The School and College Engagement team would like to extend an invitation to all colleagues who are currently acting as School Governors or Trustees in any discipline. They have established an online network to support governors and trustees with their work to share good practice, raise questions and find out more about how they can support them in their roles. There are termly meetings with guest speakers which provide a shared channel to debate pertinent topics and promote areas of discussion. If you would like to join the network, please get in touch: Contact: Sara Pittman s.pittman@exeter.ac.uk Close × Soapbox Science 2024 date - 22nd of June Exeter Quayside Soapbox Science showcases the research of women who are making significant contributions to the scientific community. The event, which takes place each summer, follows the format of London Hyde Park’s Speakers’ Corner, transforming an area of the city into an arena for public learning and scientific debate; creating a dynamic and bustling atmosphere and learning environment for all. For more information on this year’s plans and how to get involved as a presenter or volunteer see our Exeter webpage! Speakers from our Cornwall campuses are welcome too! Exeter Soapbox webpage Central Soapbox Science website You Tube: What is Soapbox Science? Close × Soup Lunch Thursdays from 12.30 to 2pm Come and enjoy a FREE LUNCH of soup and bread served by our Chaplains. Every Thursday during term-time on First Floor of Staff House. Vegetarian and vegan options will be available. Drop in any time. People from all faiths or none are warmly welcomed. More information on the Chaplaincy, other events and the Connections cafe: UoE Chaplaincy Contact: chaplaincy@exeter.ac.uk Close × Sports Park memberships and activities Explore University of Exeter gym, swim and classes membership options and fitness classes. Close × Luke'sCraft In-person South Cloisters, St Luke's Campus Every Tuesday, 12:30-13:00 Our friendly craft group has restarted, bring your own craft or use our wool supplies! Contact: Sue Whiffin s.m.whiffin@exeter.ac.uk Close × St Luke's Volunteer Gardening Group (SLUG) Wednesday lunchtimes 12.00-14.00 Everyone at St Luke’s, both staff and students, is welcome to join this group to help with the redesigning and uplifting of an area of St Luke’s campus to enhance wellbeing by providing a quiet space for staff and students to interact with green spaces and each other. Come along and do as much or as little as you like – just come and enjoy the space! The Garden can be found behind South Cloisters and is accessed by a pathway on the left-hand side just before the black side gates onto College Road. If you would like to be added to the email distribution list and be kept updated with developments, plans, events (cake sales, bulb planting etc.) please email us. Contact: StLukes_Volunteer_Garden@exeter.ac.uk Close × Tai Chi Mondays 12.30 - 13.20 There is an open, online lunchtime Chi-break class using Zoom, occasionally with a room booked on Streatham campus for staff to meet in person. Staff and students from any University of Exeter campus are welcome to join these sessions. Please note that the online class is also open to non-university members. The cost for the online classes is £7/class. Payments should please be paid to the class instructor directly.The best way to receive information about the classes, payment and Zoom details is to subscribe to the Living Movement newsletter. Please go to the Living Movement website to sign up for the newsletter. The moves of Tai Chi and Qigong are easy to learn and the low impact workout leaves you feeling good in body and mind. The classes will include gentle exercises, key moves and a little bit of short form. The classes are run by Angus Clark who is an experienced instructor, author and honorary vice-president of the Tai Chi Union of Great Britain. His website is www.livingmovement.com Contact: Anke Djordjevic a.djordjevic@exeter.ac.uk Kathryn Fyfe k.v.s.fyfe@exeter.ac.uk Close × Trans and Non-Binary Café At the Trans and Non-binary Café we offer a chance to come together with other trans people and discuss whatever you would like. Usually at some point being trans comes up but we believe there’s great value in being with other trans people, having a chance to catch up and talk and make friends with people who share the same sorts of experiences. We run a private Discord server and hold monthly in-person meetings at a wheelchair accessible location on campus. We don't share the venue or discord link publicly to protect the privacy of members but you can get these by emailing transcafe@exeter.ac.uk or if you are already in it, in the Discord server. If you are nervous of coming and would like support with it, or if you have any other questions, please do get in touch with transcafe@exeter.ac.uk, where someone from our small, all trans organising team will be happy to help. Contact: transcafe@exeter.ac.uk For more detailed information: Trans and Non-Binary Café Close × University Choral Society Mondays 7-9pm Mary Harris Memorial Chapel Open to students, staff and members of the public and welcomes singers of all levels of ability. Rehearsals are Monday evenings from 7:00-9:00pm in the Mary Harris Memorial Chapel on the Streatham Campus. Each term we hold concerts of large choral works often accompanied by student orchestras such as the University Symphony Orchestra and the University Chamber Orchestra. More info and joining instructions including memberships needed which are different for staff than for PGRs who will count as students: University Choral Society Instagram page @uoechoralsoc Close × Vegan & Vegetarian Meet-up Mondays 11.30-12.00 Term-time with ad-hoc meet-ups outside term. Hello Vegans and Vegetarian staff at the University of Exeter!!!! Let’s get together outside Reed hall (the seating area outside the cafe) at to have a chat about our experience of being vegan and/ or vegetarian in Exeter!! If the weather is nice, we can go for a little stroll around Reed pond! If wet we'll meet in the cafe inside. Get in touch to join the mailing list or for more information. Contact: Preethy Grima p.grima@exeter.ac.uk Close × Wellbeing Network We are a volunteer-led social community aiming to improve our wellbeing through positive activities and open conversations about mental health. We have a Teams group for connecting as and when, organise social "Fika" meet-ups, and other ad-hoc wellbeing positive events and activities e.g. Swing dance and yoga tasters! It's about: Open-minded conversations about how you are really feeling and doing. An opportunity for social connection. A supportive environment where all feel welcome. An invitation to come along to activities and socials. For more information about the group and our activities, to join, or to get in touch about helping us run the group see our webpage: Wellbeing Network Close × WISEnet (Women: Inspiring, Supporting, Encouraging Network) Online, hybrid and in-person Various days A new network for women has launched this year to bring together women and allies across our community. The Women: Inspiring, Supporting, Encouraging Network (WISEnet) is an inclusive and welcoming space for all women, including trans women and non-binary colleagues, to discuss relevant topics and benefit from the activities supported by the group. The network also welcomes male allies and is open to anyone that can advocate for gender equality. We run termly speaker events and have a Teams site for discussion outside of meetings. Events are hybrid to allow as many people to attend as possible. The in-person aspect of these is at Streatham campus. Find out more: WISEnet webpage Contact: wisenetwork@exeter.ac.uk Close If a correction to this page is needed or you have a question, please contact: ColleagueWellbeing@exeter.ac.uk Using our site | Accessibility | Freedom of Information | Data Protection | Copyright & disclaimer | Privacy & cookies | Cookie settings Copyright University of Exeter . Groups, networks and activities | Current staff | University of Exeter Global links Home Study Research For business Alumni Departments Visit us About us Current students International students Current staff facebook youtube instagram Search Website links Home News and updates Weekly Bulletin Rumourbuster Staff talks Faculty news Make a difference HR and employment Your employment Benefits and recognition Colleague Wellbeing Equality, diversity and inclusion Groups, networks and activities Occupational Health Volunteering and giving A-Z of services and support Campus facilities Contacts Section links Home Current staff Groups, networks and activities Groups, networks and activities All University of Exeter colleagues (current, temporary, visiting and retired) and PGRs from any of our campuses, are welcome to participate in the groups and activities listed on these pages. The fully searchable list below includes groups, networks and other activities from all campuses including ones which are online only. You could browse the whole list to see what tickles your fancy, or do a search using one of the following in the search box below and then click on the group name for more detailed information on joining etc. Campus name or broad location e.g. "Cornwall" or "St Lukes". "Online", "hybrid" or "all" for ones you can join in with from anywhere. Topic/ activity/ keyword if looking for a group on particular subject e.g. "craft" or "School Governors". Day of the week. Note - some groups may not have a set day, meet only monthly or may have activities at the weekend e.g. Hiking. Adding an existing group to this list We're happy to add existing staff-led groups that don't currently feature here unless they are one of our Research Networks as they have their own page! It's also ok to add a PGR-led group as long as it's open to staff members too. See the next section though if you want guidance on setting up a brand new group from scratch. To an existing group or network added, please get in touch via email digitalteam@exeter.ac.uk providing key information including: Name of the group, network or activity When, where and how frequently you meet up Is this in-person? If so which campus/es? Online only? Hybrid? A link to your webpages if you have one A contact email address for the listing and a name if possible Name and direct email address for the admin of this page so we can contact you regarding periodic updates. Setting up a new group You will be responsible for running the group at an administrative and practical level. This includes advertising and looking after a web page if your group has one. We'll contact you annually to check the details of your group. Please need to let us know if the regular day and time for your activities changes so we can amend the timetable/overview of all social groups. Setting up a Sharepoint site/ Teams group is a useful way to organise many groups and communicate in a more fluid way than a simple email list but this depends on the type of group you're running and what kind of admin skills/ access you have. Information is linked here on how to set up a Microsoft Teams group but contact IT if you need further support on this. We can give some advice in setting up the group and advertising if you get stuck. Some FAQs are being developed and will be added to this page as soon as they are ready. We do not usually set up webpages for individual groups. We sometimes include mention of groups in Colleague Wellbeing weekly bulletin items if it links to a campaign we are running and will contact you when we're thinking of doing this. If you wish to do a promotion drive or have a special event coming up please do get in touch. Colleague Wellbeing has no current access to budget for funding groups or other setup costs. If the group incurs costs e.g. for an instructor, this needs to be covered by the members and administration of that should be looked after by the group itself. You'll need to book your own rooms or space to run activities and carry-out any necessary risk assessments. However, do contact us if guidance or assistance is needed as we have good knowledge of University spaces and procedures at Streatham and St Lukes. Who can do this? Any PGR or staff member can set up a group on any campus. It's a good idea to make sure there enough interest from other colleagues first - we suggest a minimum of 6 people will be needed. One way to do this is to put something into the weekly bulletin asking people to get in touch with you (via email, Teams or a webform) if they are interested. Students, staff, and local residents are all welcome to join, no skills are necessary, just an interest and enthusiasm. We hold occasional social and fundraising events too. Exeter Community Garden started in 2011 as a joint initiative between the University’s grounds team and the Students’ Guild and has now evolved into a free-standing organisation managed by staff, students and local residents. The garden has 9 raised beds for vegetables, fruit and herbs, an orchard with a variety of fruit trees, together with a greenhouse, a storage building (the Observatory) and two polytunnels. As well as producing food, the Garden allows members to share skills and ideas, promotes mental wellbeing through social interaction and also allows members to look at issues of food security and sustainability, habitat protection and enhancement and the promotion of biodiversity. The Community Garden has engaged with students and academics at the University to launch the Permaculture, Growing Food with Nature MA in Food Studies based on the community garden site and using the facilities here. The course specifically investigates food production without cultivation, using sustainable products. It's more than just a coffee break; it's an inclusive social activity that promotes relaxation and socialising. The term "fika" is derived from the Swedish word "kaffe" (coffee) and is akin to the concept of a coffee break or coffee time, but it goes beyond just drinking coffee. Close × Grief, Loss and Bereavement Group Monthly online session - Wednesdays Ad-hoc in-person sessions at St Lukes and Streatham campuses This group is led and supported by the University Chaplaincy (as facilitators with Cruse training) and Colleague Wellbeing. It is a support network for colleagues and PGRs experiencing any form of grief. loss or bereavement. You could be at any stage of this experience including, for example, a recent loss, a loss some time ago, facing the future loss of someone close, a miscarriage, or the 'loss' of someone still living in the case of advanced dementia where personality change and memory loss can be common. The group is a safe space for sharing/listening and practical/reflective activities with much mutual support. We have a Teams group to share useful thoughts, feelings and resources. Our in-person or online group sessions are informal, confidential and friendly. You do not need to commit to sessions in advance and can decide not to attend if feeling too raw. You don't have to speak or even have your camera on. All engage only a much as they want and is useful to them.
